U0300.d: U0300 is the general entry of the U03xx group: the module storing it finds that its own software, calibration or configuration does not fit, or that the modules around it run versions that do not belong together. It typically follows a module swap or flash.
s: Warning lamp or MIL, depending on the module
Function of the affected module limited, e.g. suspension levelling or throttle
Code appears right after module replacement or software update
c: Module replaced without loading the latest software and configuration
Partner module left on an older software level after an update
Wrong module or part number fitted (e.g. with a replacement gearbox)
Programming aborted due to low voltage

U0301.d: U0301 means a module has found that the engine or powertrain controller carries software or a calibration it cannot work with, most often after the ECM was replaced, flashed or coded for another variant. GM's 2011 Saab 9-5 manual lists U0301 as a setup fault: tested between 9 and 16 V while the data link works, triggered by a module left unconfigured after fitting, repaired by programming rather than wiring work.
s: Check engine light or other warning lamps
Gearbox or other systems in a restricted mode
Code stored in several modules after ECM work
c: ECM/PCM replaced or flashed without configuration
ECM and TCM on different software levels after an update
ECM coded for the wrong variant or modified by tuning
Volvo: entry left behind by a service software download

U0302.d: U0302 points to a software or calibration conflict between the transmission controller and its partners. Volkswagen's 2014 Touareg and CC emission specification books show a typical trigger: the engine controller sets U0302 when it is coded for the wrong gearbox type, for instance it receives automatic transmission frames while coded for a manual, or is coded automatic in a manual car.
s: Check engine light on
Harsh or missing shifts, transmission in limp mode
Code appears after engine or transmission controller work
c: Engine controller coded for the wrong transmission type
TCM or ECM replaced or updated without matching the partner

U0303.d: U0303 reports that the transfer case control module, which engages 4WD and selects the low range, runs software or a calibration another module rejects. No manufacturer documents U0303 publicly.
s: 4WD or service 4WD warning
Shifting between 2WD, 4WD or low range refused
Code appears after transfer case module work
c: Transfer case module replaced without programming or setup
Software variant does not match the transfer case or drivetrain
Engine, transmission or body controller updated, transfer case module not

U0304.d: U0304 is stored when a control unit, usually the transmission controller, finds that the software or calibration identity of the gear shift control module does not match what it expects. GM's generic U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) treats such codes as configuration faults: checked at 9-16 V with normal bus traffic, no circuit test, cured by setup or programming.
s: Gear ranges cannot be selected or the selector does not respond
Transmission warning or code shown on the selector display
Code appears right after a selector or TCM was replaced
c: Shift selector generation or type does not match the TCM calibration (e.g. after replacement)
Shift module or TCM replaced or flashed without setup
Software update aborted, wrong file loaded

U0305.d: On current cars the cruise control module is mostly the radar unit of adaptive cruise control, which asks engine and brakes for speed changes to hold a chosen gap. U0305 is stored when another controller finds that this unit carries software or a calibration that does not belong to the vehicle, typically after a radar swap or a partial update.
s: Cruise control and adaptive distance control cannot be switched on
Driver assistance warning in the cluster, often also collision warning off
Code appears right after radar replacement, windscreen or bumper work
c: Radar/cruise module replaced or swapped from another car without programming
Wrong calibration from the factory or after an incomplete software update
Engine, brake or gateway module updated without the cruise module

U0306.d: Some diesels fire their injectors through a separate fuel injector control module that raises the voltage and opens each injector when the engine controller commands it; Ford's 6.0 L Power Stroke used such a FICM at about 48 V, and GM's 2005 Duramax table watches its injector driver by a CAN status bit that must toggle every 20 ms. U0306 means the controllers judge the module's software or calibration as not matching
s: Hard start or no start, engine may crank without firing
Rough running, misfire or reduced power
Further injector or injector module codes stored
c: Used, remanufactured or wrong-variant injector module fitted without programming
Engine controller reflashed or replaced while the injector module kept old software
Programming of the injector module interrupted, e.g. by low battery voltage

U0307.d: Glow plug control module 1 switches the glow plugs of a diesel and exchanges data with the engine controller, usually over LIN. U0307 means that the controller does not accept the module's software.
s: Long cranking or no start in cold weather
White smoke and rough idle after a cold start
MIL and glow plug warning lamp on
c: Glow plug module software outdated or not matching the engine controller
Replacement glow module of another part number or engine variant fitted
Engine controller updated or replaced without updating the glow module
Disturbed LIN line corrupting the software check

U0308.d: U0308 flags that the throttle actuator control module carries software or a calibration that the engine controller does not accept. In most current cars throttle control lives inside the ECM/PCM, so a separate TAC module and this code are rare; no manufacturer documents U0308 publicly.
s: Check engine light on
Reduced power or limp mode with limited throttle opening
Code appears after module replacement or programming
c: Throttle or engine control module replaced or flashed without matching software
Wrong or outdated calibration loaded, e.g. by an engine tune
Programming aborted due to low voltage

U0309.d: An alternative fuel control module runs the gaseous fuel side of a bi-fuel or dedicated LPG or CNG engine and works alongside the gasoline or diesel controller. CARB counts such engines as alternate-fueled vehicles that fall under OBD II.
s: Engine stays on or switches back to gasoline/diesel
MIL and gas system warning on
Rough running or hesitation in gas mode
c: Gas system module software not released for the current engine controller calibration
PCM/ECM reflashed by a dealer without updating the gas system module
Gas system module replaced with a unit of another variant

U030A.d: In some evaporative systems a dedicated module with its own pump or valve, pressure switch and electronics runs the leak test. U030A means that controller has found the module's software or calibration not to fit.
s: MIL on, usually without any drivability change
EVAP readiness monitor not completed
Further EVAP leak test codes may follow
c: Leak detection module replaced with a unit of another part number
Engine controller reprogrammed with a calibration that expects other module software
Damaged signal wire corrupting the identification exchange

U030B.d: U030B is the counterpart of U0307 for a second glow plug control module, used where an engine splits its glow plugs between two drivers, say one per bank. It is stored when the engine controller rejects the software or calibration identity of module 2, typically after only one of the two units was replaced or flashed.
s: Hard cold start, uneven running until warm
White smoke after starting in the cold
MIL and glow plug warning on
c: Only glow module 2 (or only module 1) replaced, software levels now differ
Module of another part number or engine variant installed in position 2
Engine controller updated without the second glow module

U030C.d: The reductant quality module tells the SCR system whether the tank holds proper urea solution (DEF/AdBlue); in many trucks it sits in the tank unit together with level and temperature sensing. U030C means the engine or dosing controller has rejected its software or calibration, as after a tank or sensor replacement with the wrong part number.
s: MIL and DEF/AdBlue system warning
Countdown to speed limitation or no-restart shown
Code appears after tank, heater or sensor replacement
c: DEF tank unit or quality sensor of a different part number installed
Engine or dosing controller updated, quality module left on old software
Programming interrupted or wrong file loaded

U030D.d: NOx sensor A is in most layouts the upstream sensor ahead of the SCR catalyst; its own control unit measures NOx and oxygen and sends both on CAN. U030D shows that the engine controller does not accept the software or calibration of this smart sensor, a frequent result of fitting a sensor meant for another engine or model year.
s: MIL on, SCR or emission system warning
NOx and SCR readiness monitors incomplete
Possible DEF countdown or reduced power on some trucks
c: Replacement NOx sensor of another part number or software level fitted
Aftermarket sensor whose identification the controller rejects
Engine controller updated to a calibration that expects a newer sensor

U030E.d: NOx sensor B is usually the downstream sensor after the SCR catalyst, the one whose reading reveals how well the catalyst converts and guides the correction of urea dosing. U030E is stored when its software or calibration identity does not match what the engine controller expects, for instance after a replacement sensor with another part number or a controller update the sensor does not support.
s: MIL and SCR/emission warning
SCR efficiency monitor never completes
Possible DEF countdown on some trucks
c: Downstream NOx sensor replaced with a part of another number or software level
Upstream and downstream sensors swapped or coded to the wrong position
Engine controller update requiring a newer sensor version

U030F.d: The reductant control module runs the urea side of an SCR system: pump, dosing valve, line heaters and level reading. U030F means the engine controller has found that this module's software or calibration does not belong with its own, for example after either unit was swapped or reflashed.
s: MIL and DEF/SCR warning in the cluster
Wrong or frozen DEF level display
Countdown to speed limit or reduced power
c: Dosing/reductant control unit software outdated or not released for the engine calibration
Dosing unit or DEF tank assembly with integrated controller replaced by another variant
Engine controller reprogrammed without the reductant control module

U0310.d: A fuel pump control module drives the in-tank pump at variable speed so that the pressure requested by the engine controller is reached. U0310 is set when the two controllers do not accept each other's software or calibration.
s: Hard start or no start, stalling
Hesitation, lean running or misfire under load
MIL and fuel pressure codes
c: Replacement or aftermarket pump module with software for another application
Engine controller reprogrammed, matching FPCM calibration not loaded
Interrupted programming of the pump module

U0311.d: The drive motor control module, often built into the inverter, turns battery power into phase currents for an electric traction motor and reports torque and speed. U0311 means a partner, typically the hybrid or vehicle controller, rejects the module's software or calibration.
s: Reduced propulsion power or vehicle will not drive
Hybrid/EV system warning and MIL
Jerky acceleration or one-pedal driving switched off
c: Drive motor control module software behind the level the vehicle controller expects
Only one of two drive motor modules (front/rear) updated or replaced
Inverter or drive unit replaced without programming and setup

U0312.d: Battery energy control module A supervises the high-voltage or 48 V battery: cell voltages, temperatures, current, state of charge and contactors. U0312 is stored when a partner, usually the hybrid or vehicle controller, refuses the BECM's software or calibration, for example after a pack or module replacement.
s: Hybrid/EV system warning and MIL
Electric driving or charging limited or unavailable
Engine runs more often in hybrids
c: BECM calibration outdated or not matching the hybrid controller software
Battery pack or BECM replaced without programming
Hybrid or vehicle controller updated without the BECM

U0313.d: Battery energy control module B is a second battery controller, for instance a sub-unit inside the pack that measures part of the cells for the main battery management. U0313 means the network does not accept its software or calibration.
s: Several warning lamps including MIL and hybrid system warning
Power or speed limited until the next restart
Electric operation or charging restricted
c: Sub-module software outdated or faulty, newer level required
Module B or battery section replaced with a different variant
Main battery management updated without module B

U0314.d: The four-wheel-drive clutch control module decides how much torque an on-demand coupling, such as a Haldex-type multi-plate clutch, passes to the secondary axle, using wheel speed, torque and brake data from other units. U0314 is stored when one of those partners rejects the module's software or calibration, for instance after the coupling, its controller or the engine controller was replaced or updated separately.
s: AWD/4WD warning, drive only on one axle
Reduced traction on slippery roads or when pulling away
Code appears after coupling or controller work
c: Coupling or its controller replaced without programming or coding
AWD software level not matching engine, transmission or ABS software
Used module from a vehicle with another drivetrain variant

U0315.d: U0315 concerns the ABS control module, which on most cars also hosts traction and stability control. A partner module stores the code when the brake controller's software, calibration or option configuration does not fit, typically after a module was replaced without setup.
s: ABS, traction control and stability warning lamps on
Stability and assistance functions switched off
Code present right after brake module replacement
c: ABS/EBCM replaced and not configured or programmed for the vehicle
Used unit from a vehicle with different equipment or drivetrain
Engine, steering or chassis module updated to a level the ABS unit does not support

U0316.d: U0316 means the vehicle dynamics control module, the electronic stability control unit, reports a software or calibration identity another module does not accept, typically after it was replaced or reflashed without setup. GM's U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) runs at 9-16 V and sets such codes when a module is not configured properly; GM itself uses U0315 for its electronic brake module.
s: Stability or traction control warning light on
Driver assistance functions unavailable
Code stored in several modules at once
c: Stability control module replaced or flashed without setup/coding
Software variant does not match vehicle equipment
Mazda: fault in DSC or SAS module reported to other units (U0316:09)

U0317.d: U0317 tells that the park brake control module of an electric parking brake runs software or a calibration another module does not accept. Following GM's generic U03xx logic it is checked at 9-16 V with normal bus traffic, sets when a module is not configured properly and needs no wiring test; the cure is setup or programming.
s: Park brake warning light or message
Automatic release or hill hold not working
Code appears after park brake module work
c: Park brake module replaced or flashed without setup
Mitsubishi: CAN time-out to the EPB ECU, e.g. connector unplugged
Software level of park brake module and partner module do not match

U0318.d: U0318 indicates a software or calibration mismatch with the brake system control module, a unit J2012 separates from the ABS module (U0315) and the vehicle dynamics module (U0316). Which box that is depends on the maker; on brake-by-wire systems or electromechanical boosters it is often the controller that builds brake pressure.
s: Brake system warning light or message
Brake assist or regenerative braking functions unavailable
Code appears after brake module service
c: Brake system module replaced or flashed without setup
Software level does not match the ABS/ESC or engine controller
Programming aborted due to low battery voltage

U0319.d: U0319 is set when the steering effort control module, the unit that varies steering assist, for example with road speed, reports a software or calibration identity the network does not accept. J2012 keeps it apart from the power steering control module, which has its own code U0320.
s: Steering heavier or assist no longer speed-dependent
Steering warning light or message
Code appears after steering module work
c: Steering module replaced or flashed without setup
Software variant does not match vehicle configuration
Programming aborted or wrong file loaded

U031A.d: In shift-by-wire drivelines the transmission range control module carries out the driver's range request by mechanically engaging park, reverse, neutral or drive. U031A means a partner, such as the transmission or shifter controller, rejects its software or calibration.
s: Service transmission or shift system warning
Range changes refused, car stays in Park
Wrong range shown in the display
c: TRCM calibration outdated or faulty, newer release available
TRCM/range actuator replaced without programming and learn procedure
Transmission or shifter controller updated without the TRCM

U031B.d: DC/DC converter module A moves energy between two voltage levels, in hybrids and mild hybrids typically from the high-voltage or 48 V battery to the 12 V system. U031B means another module does not accept the converter's software.
s: Often no symptom, code found during service
12 V battery or charging warning possible
Mild hybrid functions such as start-stop or recuperation limited
c: 48 V/HV battery or its management replaced by a newer version the converter software does not support
DC/DC converter replaced without programming or coding
Converter software behind the level of the other powertrain modules

U031C.d: In GM's hybrid OBD tables brake system control module B is the electromechanical brake booster (Bosch iBooster), which builds brake pressure without engine vacuum and works hand in hand with the stability control unit. The 2016 to 2019 tables describe the check behind U031C: the stability module receives a compatibility index from the booster over CAN and compares it with its own configuration.
s: MIL on and brake or stability warning in the cluster
Changed pedal feel or reduced electric brake boost
Code appears right after brake booster or ESP module work
c: Brake booster unit replaced or swapped without programming to the vehicle
Stability control module updated or configured for another booster variant
Programming interrupted, for example by low battery voltage

U031D.d: Parking assist control module A evaluates the ultrasonic bumper sensors for park distance warnings and, on newer vehicles, supports low-speed helpers such as automated parking. U031D tells that another controller considers the software or configuration of this module wrong for the vehicle.
s: Wrench lamp or service message without any drivability complaint
Park distance warning or trailer hitch assist not available
Code returns after clearing until the configuration is corrected
c: Vehicle or PCM configuration lists a parking or trailer feature that does not match the fitted module
Parking assist module replaced or swapped without programming
Only some modules updated, leaving the parking module on an older level

U031E.d: Parking assist control module B is a second park aid unit, found where front and rear sensors are split between controllers or an automatic parking controller sits beside the distance warning; which unit gets the letter B is decided by each maker. U031E is set when a partner module rejects the software or setup of module B, mostly after a replacement or an incomplete update.
s: Park assist unavailable message in the cluster
No warning tones from front or rear sensors
Automatic parking function cannot be started
c: Second parking module replaced or taken from another car without programming
Module variant does not match the fitted sensor set or parking option
Software update of the parking module interrupted or incomplete

U031F.d: The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) is the SYNC computer, as Ford calls it, behind the centre screen, which handles audio sources, phone, voice control and navigation. U031F tells that a connected unit finds the APIM software unsuitable.
s: Centre screen stays dark or keeps rebooting
No radio, phone or navigation functions
Rear camera picture or touch controls missing on the screen
c: Replacement display or other unit needs a newer SYNC software level than installed
APIM replaced or swapped without module installation and configuration
SYNC update interrupted or installed only partly

U0320.d: The power steering control module drives the electric assist motor and needs calibration data that suit the steering gear and the vehicle. U0320 is logged when another module refuses to work with its software.
s: Steering heavy or assist only partly available
Power steering warning lamp or message
Lane keeping or park steering functions switched off
c: Steering gear or steering module replaced without loading matching calibration
Steering module software older than required by the other modules
Basic setting or adaptation after programming not carried out

U0321.d: Suspension control module A manages adjustable dampers, air springs or ride height, and on some cars it also leads active roll control; some code lists call it the ride level module. U0321 tells that a partner controller considers its software unfit.
s: Suspension warning in the cluster
Ride height cannot be adjusted or vehicle sits at one level
Firm or uneven damping, more body roll
c: Replacement suspension or roll control unit carries a software level the partners do not accept
Only one of the linked chassis modules updated
Suspension module coded for another equipment level

U0322.d: The body control module switches lighting, locks, wipers and many comfort functions and often holds configuration data used by other units. U0322 tells that a controller has found the BCM software or setup unfit for the vehicle.
s: Headlamps, interior lights or wipers work wrongly or not at all
Central locking or remote key functions unreliable
Several body codes stored at the same time
c: BCM replaced or swapped without loading vehicle configuration
BCM updated while a connected unit such as a headlamp module kept old software
BCM programming interrupted by low voltage or lost connection

U0323.d: The instrument panel control module is the cluster with gauges, warning lamps and messages; it also passes data such as units or outside temperature to other modules. U0323 means the engine controller or another unit rejects its software or coding.
s: MIL or several warning lamps such as TPMS and stability control on
Codes in engine, ABS and cluster that cannot be cleared
Outside temperature or other displays missing
c: Cluster not coded for the fitted equipment, for example the ambient temperature sensor
Start-up exchange interrupted by a missing fuse, disconnected infotainment unit or quick ignition off
Retrofitted accessory such as an alarm kit disturbing the cluster data
Cluster replaced or updated without matching configuration

U0324.d: The HVAC control module reads cabin and outside temperatures and drives blend doors, blower, defrosting and the request for the A/C compressor. U0324 means another controller has found its software or calibration unfit for the vehicle.
s: Heating, cooling or defrosting works only in part
Climate settings reset or remote start climate stays off
A/C compressor not requested
c: HVAC module calibration outdated or not matching the vehicle options
Connected part replaced, such as antenna, display or compressor, without matching HVAC software
HVAC module replaced or taken from another car without setup

U0325.d: The auxiliary heater control module runs an extra heat source: a fuel-burning or electric coolant heater, or on electrified cars a high-voltage heater that warms the cabin while the engine is off. U0325 means a connected module rejects this unit's software.
s: No auxiliary or parking heat, cabin warms only with the engine running
Heater warning or service message
On plug-in hybrids the engine starts more often for heat
c: Heater unit or its controller replaced without programming or coding
Climate or vehicle software level does not match the heater variant
Retrofitted parking heater not coded into the vehicle network

U0326.d: The vehicle immobilizer control module checks the transponder or smart key and releases the engine controller only after a coded exchange. U0326 means that a controller, usually the engine controller, does not accept the immobilizer's software or stored codes, mostly once either unit has been renewed or reprogrammed.
s: Engine cranks but does not start, or starts and stalls at once
Security or key lamp flashes in the cluster
Keys are not recognised after module work
c: Engine controller or immobilizer unit replaced without pairing the security codes
Used module from another vehicle fitted, carrying foreign codes
Software of engine controller and immobilizer on incompatible levels after an update

U0327.d: The vehicle security control module handles theft protection: alarm, monitoring of doors, bonnet and tailgate and, at some makers, the key check that unlocks the engine. Chrysler, for example, gives this job to its wireless control module, and its lost-contact code U0168 calls that unit the vehicle security control module (18-023-13).
s: No start or start refused although the key is accepted at the door
Alarm triggers without reason or cannot be armed
Security lamp flashing, remote locking unreliable
c: Security or wireless control module replaced without programming and key learning
Engine or body controller updated while the security module kept old software
Aftermarket alarm or remote start interfering with the security data

U0328.d: The steering angle sensor module reports wheel angle and turning speed over CAN, mainly to stability control and electric power steering. U0328 means a receiving module rejects the software or variant of this sensor.
s: ESC, traction control or lane assist warning lamps on
Steering assist uneven or the car pulls after alignment work
Code appears after wheel alignment or steering column repair
c: Steering angle sensor or column part replaced without calibration or setup
Sensor of another part number or software variant fitted
Brake or steering module software does not support the fitted sensor

U0329.d: The steering column control module gathers the stalks and wheel buttons for indicators, wipers, horn and cruise control, and on newer cars it may also handle the heated wheel or pass on the steering angle. U0329 means a partner module rejects the software of this unit.
s: Indicators, wipers or horn work only partly
Cruise control or wheel buttons without reaction
Assistance functions using steering column signals unavailable
c: Replacement steering column module of the wrong variant fitted
Module installation or programming after replacement not completed
Steering column module software older than the connected modules expect

U032A.d: The A/C compressor control module drives an electric refrigerant compressor, as used in hybrid and electric cars, and reports speed and status to the climate controller. U032A means that controller considers the compressor module's software or learned data invalid.
s: Air conditioning blows warm, compressor does not run
Fault returns after a while even when cooling was restored
On electric cars battery cooling or preconditioning may be limited
c: Compressor module lost its adaptation and needs the calibration routine
Climate or compressor software below the level of an open update campaign
Electric compressor replaced without programming and calibration

U0330.d: The tyre pressure monitor module receives the radio messages of the wheel sensors, evaluates the pressures and, on many systems, works out which sensor sits on which wheel; from this it drives the warning lamp and cluster messages. U0330 is set when a partner controller finds the software or variant of this module unsuitable, usually after a replacement or a partial update.
s: Tyre pressure warning lamp or TPMS fault message in the cluster
Tyre pressures not shown or shown on the wrong wheel
Code appears after work on the TPMS module or a software update
c: TPMS module replaced or taken from another vehicle without programming and coding
Module still on a software level that the partner controllers no longer accept
Module configured for another wheel, tyre or sensor variant

U0331.d: Body control module A is the first of several body controllers on vehicles that spread lighting, locking, wipers and power distribution over more than one unit. With a single body controller the same mismatch is reported as U0322; U0339 covers unit B.
s: Lighting, locking or wiper functions fail or behave oddly
Keyless start or remote locking may not work
Several modules store network codes after body module work
c: Body control module A replaced without loading the vehicle configuration
Programming aborted or corrupted by an outdated diagnostic tool release
Other body modules updated while unit A stayed on its old level

U0332.d: Multi-axis acceleration sensor module A measures yaw rate plus lateral and longitudinal acceleration for stability control and driver assistance; it can be a separate box or part of another controller. U0332 means a receiving controller rejects its software or variant.
s: Stability control or traction control warning lamp on
Driver assistance functions unavailable
Code follows module replacement or software update
c: Sensor module replaced by a part with another software or variant
Brake or suspension controller updated without matching the sensor module
Yaw rate sensor learn skipped after programming

U0333.d: With shift-by-wire, both the driver's selector and the unit that actually moves the range are electronic modules; module B denotes a second such unit, either a further selector or the shift actuator. U0333 means its software or calibration does not fit the partner controller.
s: Range changes requested at this unit are ignored
Transmission warning or shift indicator fault
Vehicle stays in or returns to neutral or park
c: Selector or actuator of another generation or part number fitted
Transmission calibration specifies a different selector than the one fitted
Shift actuator ECU still on an outdated calibration

U0334.d: On current vehicles the radio is the infotainment head unit: besides audio it runs navigation, voice control, phone connection and the setting menus for other systems such as seat heating. U0334 is stored when a controller relying on these services rejects the radio's software.
s: No sound or missing functions on the head unit
Comfort settings shown greyed out in the radio menus
Code appears after a radio update or replacement
c: Radio update done out of sequence or with a skipped intermediate level
Head unit replaced by a variant for another market or equipment
Other modules updated while the radio stayed on an old level

U0335.d: The battery pack sensor module is housed in the traction battery, where it measures pack current and voltage for the battery controller. U0335 records that this controller or another partner rejects the module's software.
s: Vehicle will not enter ready mode or drives with reduced power
Charging does not start or stops early
Range and state of charge shown incorrectly
c: Battery controller updated without matching the sensor module, or the reverse
Sensor module or contactor box replaced with a part on another software level
Programming of the battery modules interrupted

U0336.d: The restraints control module reads the crash sensors and triggers airbags and belt tensioners according to a calibration written for one body style and equipment level. U0336 means a connected unit rejects the software or configuration of this module.
s: Airbag warning lamp stays on
Further restraint codes such as airbag circuit faults stored
Code appears right after airbag module replacement
c: Replacement airbag module delivered with an older software level and not brought up to the vehicle level
Calibration for another body style, drive or equipment loaded
Used module from another vehicle installed

U0337.d: Battery charger control module A is the charger built into a plug-in car: it turns mains AC into DC for the traction battery and coordinates with the charging station and the battery controller. U0337 appears when a partner module refuses the charger's software or calibration.
s: Charging does not start or stops after a short time
Charging fault message that clears only after replugging
12 V battery drained after charging sessions
c: On-board charger left on an older software level after other modules were updated
Charger replaced without programming to the vehicle
Charger update interrupted, for example by low 12 V supply

U0338.d: The remote function actuation module receives key fob, passive entry and, on newer cars, phone key signals and passes lock, unlock or start requests to the body controller. U0338 means a partner rejects its software.
s: Remote or keyless locking does not respond
Keyless start refused or key not detected
Module not reachable by the diagnostic tool after replacement
c: Replacement module shipped with software for another network layout
Software download aborted by low voltage, a lost link or a corrupted file
Module fitted but not configured or keys not programmed

U0339.d: Body control module B is a second body controller that takes over part of the switching, for example in a rear or auxiliary junction box. U0339 means a partner module rejects its software or setup; U0331 covers unit A, U0322 vehicles with a single body controller.
s: Functions switched by the second body module fail, such as lights or sill plate illumination
Depending on its tasks, engine may stall or not start
Network codes in several modules after body module work
c: Body control module B carries a configuration that does not match the vehicle
Unit B left on an older software level after an update campaign
Auxiliary junction box replaced without programming

U033A.d: U033A is the one code of this row that a manufacturer names in public. Volvo's bulletins for the battery-electric VNR Electric truck (KC-2288 of 2023, CBR-2288 of June 2024, the latter also valid for the Mack LRe) list it among faults that turn active right after the ESCM has been reprogrammed, together with missing-message codes for interface modules A to D.
s: Code turns active directly after a module programming session
Missing-message codes for interface modules A to D stored at the same time
High-voltage battery warning until the battery unit is reprogrammed
c: Battery management unit left on its old software after another controller was reprogrammed
Programming session ended before all battery-related units were flashed
Interface module A replaced and not brought to the matching level

U033B.d: Module B is the second interface board, and on GM's eAssist mild hybrids it is also the last: bulletin PIT5513D lists exactly two, K112A and K112B, for 2016–2018 Silverado and Sierra and the 2018 LaCrosse, both under the same part number 24282084. Since one spare fits either slot, the part number alone does not tell which position a board serves.
s: Hybrid system or battery warning, often with the check engine lamp on PHEVs
Electric assist or electric driving reduced
Fault follows work on the battery pack
c: Board B replaced with a spare carrying another software level
Battery controller software older than the board it has to accept
Identical boards A and B swapped during pack repair

U033C.d: U033C names the third interface board. GM's closest published check is its own code P1EB1 in the VITM of the Volt: at power-up the controller compares its own software version with that of all slave boards and logs P1EB1 if any one does not fit, within 200 ms, with at least 9 V and no slave lost-communication fault active.
s: MIL possible on hybrids, as GM rates its comparable check Type A
Hybrid or high-voltage battery warning after switching on
Electric driving or charging restricted
c: Board C carries a software version the battery controller does not list as compatible
Battery controller updated while the boards stayed on the old level
Unstable low-voltage supply at power-up corrupts the version exchange

U033D.d: On the first-generation Chevrolet Volt the monitoring electronics end at the fourth board. GM's 2012 Volt table refers to four slave units through its own codes: P1EB2 to P1EB5 report a slave that answered wrongly or not at all when a programming session ended, and U2603 to U2606, listed in GM's U-code catalogue for the 2011 Saab 9-4X as loss of hybrid battery interface control modules 1 to 4, block the software comp
s: Code appears after programming or replacing a battery section
Hybrid warning, MIL possible on plug-in hybrids
Reduced propulsion until all boards match
c: Programming of the fourth board aborted or answered with an error
Replacement board D still on a superseded software version
Interrupted link to board D masks or disturbs the version check

U033E.d: A fifth interface board exists, for example, in BMW's 330e plug-in hybrid of the F30 series: bulletin SI B61 25 17 lists voltage-measurement codes for cell supervision circuits 1 to 5 in the battery electronics SME, under BMW's own numbers 21F0C2 to 21F0C6. BMW replaces a CSC only if the fault is active, has been logged five times, or twice with the MIL lit, and once harness and cell voltages have been checked.
s: Powertrain or hybrid warning, MIL possible on plug-in hybrids
Fault stored after a battery or BMS repair
Electric range or power temporarily limited
c: Fifth supervision board replaced without matching the controller software
Battery controller not updated to the part numbers now installed
Boards of different production levels combined in one pack

U033F.d: Public documents name no vehicle that uses U033F, nor a pack with exactly six interface boards; F is simply the sixth address in the row. What is documented is how strictly battery software must follow the hardware.
s: Limp-home mode or reduced electric power
Stop/start or electric assist disabled
Battery or hybrid warning after battery service
c: Battery parameters not updated after a pack or module replacement
Board F taken from another pack with a different software level
Battery controller on an outdated calibration

U0340.d: G is the seventh board, a position GM's 2016–2019 plug-in hybrids really have: table 16OBDG02 describes eight interface modules on a UART daisy chain to the battery system module. That table publishes lost-contact and processor tests for every board, yet it holds no counterpart to the P1EB1 version check of the older VITM design and no U0340.
s: Hybrid warning, MIL possible depending on the maker
Electric mode limited or unavailable
Other battery diagnostics paused while the code is active
c: Seventh board replaced by a unit with another software level
Battery system module reflashed without the boards being brought along
Disturbed daisy-chain link garbles the version data of board G

U0341.d: Packs with eight boards end at H. Besides GM's 2016–2019 plug-ins, BMW's i3 is one: bulletin SI B61 02 16 lists eight cell supervision circuits for the i3 battery and, for boards built between December 2013 and September 2014, orders all of them renewed together once diagnosis calls for a CSC.
s: Car cannot be made ready to drive
Code set after battery section work
Drive power reduced
c: Software of the last board does not match after a section replacement
Only some boards renewed where the maker requires a complete set
Service tool, adapter or tool software of the wrong generation used

U0342.d: Mitsubishi shows that a replaced monitoring board must first be given its place in the pack. On the 2022 Outlander plug-in hybrid, numbering of the cell monitoring units (CMU) is done at the factory; after a CMU or battery module has been replaced, the workshop runs CMU ID numbering from the battery management unit with the M.U.T.-III tester, never while the battery is charging, and checks that every ID data item rea
s: Battery warning after a module or CMU replacement
EV mode or charging restricted
MIL possible on plug-in hybrids
c: Replaced board not numbered or registered in the battery controller
ID numbering run while charging or aborted before completion
Board of another battery variant fitted at position I

U0343.d: J, the tenth board, only appears on larger packs. BMW's i8 is a documented example with more than ten: the parts list in bulletin SI B61 02 16 counts twelve cell monitoring circuits, and the battery electronics SME carries a voltage plausibility code for each of them, numbered 1 to 12 (21F0F3 to 21F0FE).
s: Car will not become ready to drive
High-voltage system switches off, contactor opens
Drivetrain malfunction message
c: Tenth board carries software the battery controller does not accept
Replacement boards from different production batches combined
Internal battery bus disturbs the identification of board J

U0344.d: Eleven boards or more are found in GM's Ultium packs: according to Wikipedia the Cadillac Lyriq carries twelve modules and the Hummer EV two layers of twelve, and the battery management works wirelessly. GM's service update N232401570 of October 2025 shows that master software decides whether such a unit is accepted: on 2023–2024 Lyriq and BrightDrop, 2024 Blazer EV and Silverado EV and 2022–2024 Hummer EV, the batte
s: Vehicle does not become ready after switching on
Battery or propulsion warning
Charging may be refused
c: Battery controller software does not accept the monitoring unit
Released software update for the battery controller not yet installed
Monitoring unit K replaced and not registered

U0345.d: L is the twelfth letter and thus the last board on packs with twelve, such as the twelve CSCs of BMW's i8, provided a maker counted them this way. The mismatch behind U0345 is easy to create during battery repair.
s: Hybrid warning after high-voltage battery replacement
Electric assist reduced
MIL possible on hybrids
c: Battery controller logic and pack generation do not match
Update for new-generation packs applied to an old-generation pack
Twelfth board replaced with a unit of another software level

U0346.d: With M the row passes the common twelve-board size. GM's 2018 hybrid table 18OBDG02 includes lost-contact codes for interface modules up to M (U01AC) in its bundle BICM Loss of Comm and adds that GM shares software across programs, so a code counts only where the program in question uses it.
s: Battery or propulsion warning
Power or charging limited
Code seen only on very large packs
c: Thirteenth board on a software level the controller rejects
Controller software variant for another pack configuration
Board installed in the wrong layer or position of a multi-layer pack

U0347.d: N, the fourteenth slot, is not tied to any vehicle in public sources. What can be shown is how false mismatch codes arise in the workshop.
s: Code appears during or right after a tester session
Further network codes in the battery controller
Often no change in driving once programming is completed
c: Stale or incorrectly started tester session reports a false mismatch
Programmable module installation skipped after a battery replacement
Board N really carries incompatible software

U0348.d: O stands for a fifteenth board; no public document links U0348 to a vehicle. That the software inside a cell monitoring unit can itself be the problem is shown by Honda's recall 15V602 of October 2015: in 6,786 Accord Hybrids of 2014–2015 the cell voltage sensor (CVS) could misread electrical noise from inverter and motor circuits, a side effect of a change made for digital TV reception in Japan, and switch the car i
s: Fail-safe mode with reduced speed and power
Engine switched off, electric drive only until the battery is drained
Hybrid warning with audible alert
c: Firmware of the monitoring unit itself faulty and superseded
Board O missed a released software update
Pack boards on different update levels after a partial repair

U0349.d: P is the sixteenth and final letter; the following number, U034A, already names an engine disconnect clutch, so a pack with more than sixteen boards would need maker codes. No vehicle is publicly linked to U0349.
s: Software updates fail or are not offered
Battery warning after battery service
Charging or power limited in severe cases
c: Battery firmware so old that over-the-air updates cannot be applied
Sixteenth board replaced without matching software
Code confused with U034A, which belongs to another component

U034A.d: Parallel hybrids place a disconnect clutch between combustion engine and electric drive; it couples the engine in or separates it for electric driving. Where the clutch has its own actuator controller, U034A means the hybrid or transmission controller rejects that unit's software.
s: Engine warning lamp or transmission warning on
Electric driving or engine start-stop unavailable
Harsh engagement or loss of drive until the next key cycle
c: Hybrid, engine and transmission controllers on software levels that do not belong together
Clutch actuator or transmission unit replaced without programming
Programming of a powertrain module interrupted

U034B.d: Brake booster control is the electromechanical brake servo that replaces the vacuum booster and lets regenerative braking be blended in; in the VW group it is unit J539, which holds the pedal travel sensor and the motor position sensor (self-study 861213). Audi documents U034B00 on the 2025 A3 and S3: with servo software 0562 the unit logs U034B00 with symptom 500032 during the start phase, the engine controller adds
s: Engine warning lamp stays on after starting
Request-MIL code stored in the engine controller
Code returns after clearing until new booster software is installed
c: Faulty software level in the electromechanical brake booster
Brake booster unit replaced without programming or coding
Brake or engine controller updated without matching the booster

U034C.d: Battery energy control module C is a third battery controller, found where a high-voltage battery is split into sections with their own management electronics. U034C means the leading controller or another partner rejects its software.
s: Reduced drive power or no ready mode
Charging refused or slower than usual
High-voltage system warning in the cluster
c: Battery controllers on software levels that do not match each other or the vehicle controller
Battery section or its controller replaced without programming
Battery software update aborted or only partly applied

U034D.d: The vehicle thermal management control module commands pumps, valves and fans that keep battery, drive electronics and cabin at their target temperatures. U034D means a partner controller rejects its software or calibration.
s: Weak cabin heating or cooling
Charging or drive power limited to protect the battery
Warning lamp with thermal or coolant codes stored
c: Thermal management controller on an outdated software level
Thermal management module replaced without programming
High-voltage heater or another partner updated without matching the thermal controller

U034E.d: Active grille air shutter modules are small actuator controllers, usually LIN slaves of the engine controller, that open and close flaps in the front end to speed up warm-up and cut drag. U034E means the engine controller refuses the software of shutter module A.
s: Check engine lamp may light depending on the maker
Upper grille flaps stay open or closed
Slower engine warm-up in cold weather
c: Shutter actuator with an unsuitable firmware level fitted
Shutter assembly for another engine or model year installed
Engine controller updated to a level that expects a different shutter

U034F.d: Shutter module B is the second flap actuator; at GM it drives the lower shutter. U034F tells that its software or variant differs from what the engine controller has stored as valid, typically after a shutter with another part number or firmware was fitted.
s: Lower grille flaps no longer move
Check engine lamp may light depending on the maker
Code appears after a lower shutter was replaced
c: Lower shutter actuator with early or unsuitable firmware
Lower shutter replaced by a part with another part number
Water in the lower connector disturbing the module and misread as a software fault

U0350.d: Module C denotes one more flap actuator with its own bus address, needed where the front end splits its air openings into more sections, for example left and right lower flaps. U0350 indicates that the engine controller does not accept this unit's software.
s: Air flap warning message in the cluster
One group of flaps remains in its last position
Check engine lamp may light depending on the maker
c: Side or lower flap actuator with another part number or firmware fitted
Left and right actuators swapped or mixed between model versions
Engine controller software expects a different shutter configuration

U0351.d: Shutter module D is the fourth address the code list reserves for grille flap actuators and is relevant only where a front end has four independently driven flap groups. U0351 signals that the engine controller will not accept the software of that unit.
s: One flap group no longer opens or closes
Air flap warning or check engine lamp depending on the maker
No noticeable change in driving
c: Flap actuator of group D with another part number or firmware fitted
Front end or bumper from another version fitted with different shutter equipment
Engine controller calibration expects a different number of shutter modules

U0352.d: NOx sensor C is a third smart NOx sensor with its own electronics, fitted on exhaust systems with a second SCR stage, where it watches the gas behind the last catalyst. U0352 means the engine controller declines the software or calibration of this sensor, for example after a part meant for another engine or model year was fitted.
s: Check engine lamp possible, depending on the maker's rating
SCR or catalyst readiness does not complete
Code appears right after a NOx sensor replacement
c: NOx sensor for another engine, model year or position fitted
Engine controller updated to a level that expects another sensor software
Sensor C swapped with the sensor of another position

U0353.d: An ion sense module places a small voltage across the plug gap after each spark and turns the resulting ion current into combustion, knock and misfire information for the engine controller; Ford's patent US20170030322A1 shows such a unit inside the ignition system. U0353 says the engine controller has found software or a calibration in this module that does not match its own, typically after a module swap or a one-si
s: Check engine light
Misfire or knock codes stored at the same time
Code appears right after a module replacement or reflash
c: Engine controller or ion sense module updated without the matching partner software
Replacement ion sense module with another part number or calibration
Programming of one of the two units interrupted or incomplete

U0354.d: The inductive charger control module is the on-board part of a wireless charging system: a receiving coil under the floor picks up energy from a ground pad, and the module rectifies it and coordinates the process with battery management and charge controller. U0354 is stored when one of those partners finds that the module runs software or a calibration it does not accept, say after an exchange or a partial update.
s: Wireless charging does not start
Charging warning in the display while cable charging still works
c: Inductive charger module replaced but not programmed or configured
Battery or charge controller updated to a level that expects other charger software
Software update of the charger module aborted
